Thanks for the metadata, Priya — quick technical notes ahead of tomorrow’s call so we can focus on the scoping items:

SSO/SAML
- We consume standard SAML 2.0 metadata (entityID, SSO binding). The x509 cert is enough for us to validate incoming assertions; we support both HTTP-POST and HTTP-Redirect bindings.
- Assertion attributes we typically look for: email (primary), name, and a group claim if present. If your Okta sends group="memberOf" we can map to Redwood teams.

SCIM
- Redwood supports SCIM 2.0 with full CRUD and incremental delta. We recommend the following attribute map (attached CSV):
  - userName -> emails[0].value
  - externalId -> acme:employeeId
  - name.givenName / familyName
  - title -> jobTitle
  - urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User -> department
  - groups -> memberOf (for OKTA group push)
- Provisioning token: we can accept a bearer token for SCIM; token rotation is supported via our API (rotate endpoints documented). If you prefer certificate-based mutual TLS for provisioning we can support that in Private deployments — please confirm which model you prefer.

Service accounts / tokens
- For hosted customers we recommend a scoped service-account token named like redwood-acme-scim-provisioner. For Dedicated/Private we support mTLS service certs. Token expiry and rotation: default is 90 days, support automation via /tokens/rotate.

IP allowlist
- For Hosted API: we have a published set of static egress CIDRs per region (we’ll provide the list). For Dedicated: you can use private peering and static LAN ranges; for Private we run entirely on your VPC.

I attached scim-attribute-mapping.csv with the exact column names we’ll use for the mapping. On the call I’ll run through a test provisioning flow and create a test user in your Okta sandbox.

- Priya/Rajesh: confirm which Okta groups map to Redwood teams and share a sample user JSON.
- Dev: provide Hosted CIDR list (will attach in follow-up).
